Flood Insurance Data

Outside the zone: paid flood claims rated outside high-risk zones

In FEMA's records for losses 2016–2025, 26.6% of 461,197 claims with a payment and a rated zone across all U.S. counties combined were rated outside zones A and V; across the 364 counties with at least 100 each, 25.9% (90% range 19.0–32.7%, resampling counties). Across those counties, a county's claim share and its share of policy units outside zones A and V go together (correlation 0.70, descriptive, no test), so compare the two columns.

FEMA's own figure: over the 10 years 2014 to 2024, nearly one-third (29%) of NFIP flood insurance claims came from areas outside of current high-risk flood areas. (FloodSmart.) FEMA's figure uses current high-risk areas and the years 2014 to 2024, and does not say whether it counts only paid claims; this page counts paid claims by the zone rated on each claim.

By Michael Woo, publisher of Flood Insurance Data (about the site), who works with data, is not an insurance agent, adjuster or engineer, and answers for every figure here. Written with AI tools; every row is recomputed from FEMA's records by a separate check before publishing. First published 2026-11-13; data as of August 31, 2026.

Abstract

Data: 364 counties with at least 100 claims with a payment and a rated zone each (424,932 in all), from FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP Claims v3, losses 2016–2025, as of August 31, 2026.

Result: across those counties, 25.9% (90% range 19.0–32.7%, resampling counties) of claims with a payment and a rated zone were rated outside zones A and V; the median county's share is 25.6%. The highest share is Montgomery County, MD at 97.0% (130 of 134); the lowest share, 0.0%, is Holt County, MO (0 of 246).

Question

In which U.S. counties are the most paid NFIP flood claims rated outside FEMA's high-risk zones (A and V)? The measure is the share of paid NFIP claims with a rated flood zone whose zone is outside zones A and V (zones X, B, C and D).

Data

FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP Claims v3 (API) records as of August 31, 2026, FEMA fields ratedFloodZone, netBuildingPaymentAmount, netContentsPaymentAmount, netIccPaymentAmount, yearOfLoss, nonPaymentReasonBuilding. Base: NFIP claims on every building type with a loss in the window, a payment above $0 and a rated flood zone; zone D (possible but undetermined hazard) counts as outside A and V; records FEMA coded deleted or assigned in error left out.

Methods

The share is the number of claims with a payment and a rated zone that were rated outside zones A and V, divided by all claims with a payment and a rated zone in the county FEMA codes on the record, both counted from the same records. A county is listed only with at least 100 claims with a payment and a rated zone. Left out: 2,042 counties with fewer than 100 claims with a payment and a rated zone and 621 with none; across the 2,042 left-out counties with at least one, the median share of paid claims outside zones A and V is 33.3% and the pooled share 34.7%, so the listed counties are not a sample of every county. Intervals, fifths, the county-resampling range, records left out and why no test is run: shared methods for every paper.

Results

  • Pooled over the 364 counties: 25.9% (90% range 19.0–32.7%) of 424,932 claims with a payment and a rated zone; the 2,042 counties left out pool to 34.7%.
  • Median county: 25.6%. Highest: Montgomery County, MD, 97.0% (90% range 93.5–98.7%).
  • 19 of the 50 counties with the highest share of paid claims outside zones A and V are in Texas, which has 32 of the 364 listed counties.

Prior work

No national ranking of counties on this base was found in searches on 2026-11-12. Penn State's PSIRC mapped Pennsylvania NFIP claims, including claims outside the Special Flood Hazard Area, from FEMA's 2019 claims release. FEMA's own figure is set beside this one at the top of the page.

Limitations

  • This is a share of claims, not of homes, and not the chance that any home floods.
  • The zone is the zone FEMA rated on the claim, which can differ from today's map.
  • Claims with no rated zone are not in the base.
  • Only NFIP records: private flood insurance is not in FEMA's data.
  • A fifth is a position in this list, not a grade, a risk score or a prediction.

Reproduce

Download every record from FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP Claims v3, keep the claims with a payment and a rated zone for losses 2016–2025, group by the county FEMA codes, count the base and the records meeting the measure, drop counties under 100, and compute each share of paid claims outside zones A and V with a 90% Wilson interval (z = 1.6449), checking against the CSV, which gives every numerator and denominator.

How to cite

Michael Woo, Flood Insurance Data, "Outside the zone: paid flood claims rated outside high-risk zones," NFIP losses 2016–2025, data as of August 31, 2026, https://floodinsurancedata.com/flood-insurance/outside-the-zone/. This product uses FEMA's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

Versions

This is a fixed copy of the version with data as of August 31, 2026; it is not changed by later refreshes. The current version has the latest data.

Corrections

No corrections so far. Report a figure that looks wrong to contact@floodinsurancedata.com; every correction is listed here with its date.
